fixes.explanation: I can see why you'd think that, friend, but authority isn't the gift named here. The Son of God "…has given us understanding, so that we may know Him who is true…" (1 John 5:20) The gift is understanding, and its aim is knowing Him, not being in charge of anything. Then the verse says "…we are in Him who is true…" So knowing Him and being in Him sit side by side.

I see why you'd pick that, baker, but strong drink isn't named in this verse. Right before it, the writer says of Jesus Christ, "He is the true God and eternal life." (1 John 5:20) Then comes the closing line, "Little children, keep yourselves from idols." (1 John 5:21) I think those two lines sit together on purpose. Once the letter has pointed to the true God, an idol is something set up in His place, so the last word is to keep away from those.

problems.problem: The explanation restates that understanding is given so believers may know Him, but does not develop that connection.
The explanation points out that the mention of idols follows the statement about the true God, but does not explain the significance of that connection.
